clue.text: Some boots have these laces

explanation.surface: A remark about footwear: some boots come with laces.
explanation.definitionFit: Running shoes and football boots carry metal studs on the sole, and to lace a drink is to add alcohol to it, which is also called spiking it.

clue.text: Seek prey — that's extremely popular with nocturnal hunter

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the first and last letters of popular are taken

parts.note: the owl is a bird that hunts at night

explanation.surface: An animal hunting at night that is very well liked by the owls.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to roam stealthily in search of something to catch, as a predator does.

clue.text: Warwick draughts champion?

explanation.surface: Warwick is presented as someone who excels at the board game draughts.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, was nicknamed the Kingmaker in the Wars of the Roses. In draughts (checkers) a piece reaching the far row is crowned a king, so a strong player makes many.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Warwick earned the title by putting Edward IV and later Henry VI on the throne; a skilled checkers player keeps crowning pieces.

clue.text: Such a tedious farewell

parts.note: such, as in 'such a fool', can be replaced by so
something tedious seems long or drawn-out

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a goodbye that drags on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase is an informal way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Nobody comes to opening of this poor show

parts.note: nobody means not one person, none
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: Nobody turns up to the first night of this disappointing production.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion that turns out disappointing or insignificant is called a damp squib or flop.

clue.text: A good idea at last. I hear you utter

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges that the other person is finally speaking sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is said in approval of a welcome suggestion; read literally, it simply observes that the listener is speaking at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom greets a proposal one likes after poorer ones, and literally it states that the other person is speaking at present.

clue.text: Two boys, and not a girl, in France

parts.note: Norm is a boy's name, short for Norman
Andy is a boy's name, short for Andrew

explanation.surface: Two lads, and not a single girl, are in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and not a girl' steers the solver off the girl's name Norma, which also starts the answer. The region is defined loosely as a place in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The region lies on the Channel coast of northern France, site of the 1944 landings.

clue.text: There's nothing of the animal in him

definitions.text: There's nothing of the animal in him

parts.words: There's nothing of the animal in him
parts.note: seemingly praise of a gentle, civilised man, but literally someone who eats no meat, milk or other animal product

explanation.definitionFit: A strict vegetarian eats and uses no animal products at all.

clue.text: Gains a lot in travel, but has desire in return

indicators.note: the letters are sent travelling, moving to new places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A journey brings great profit, yet the traveller still longs to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in travel' signals the anagram of GAINS A LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Greek for homecoming and pain: a wistful longing to go back to an earlier time or place.

clue.text: A cliché: say, the Danube is blue

parts.note: corn is trite, hackneyed material, as in corny
a river is something that flows, so the Danube is an example of a flower

explanation.surface: Calling the Danube blue is a hackneyed phrase, as in the famous waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' here is a thing that flows, i.e. a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The shade is named after the bright blue wild plant of cornfields.

clue.text: With difficulty, breathe air quietly

parts.note: air is a gas
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone struggles for breath and takes in air softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to draw breath sharply and with effort.

clue.text: Ardent with love for bird

parts.note: ardent, like flaming, means burning or passionate
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone passionate in love goes for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink long-legged wading species is one example of a bird.

clue.text: Render ineffective a buried type of seed

indicators.note: a is buried, set down inside the word for render ineffective

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or make void

explanation.surface: A seed is buried so that it will not grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried' puts A inside ANNUL, after its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed packets are sold by the plant's life cycle, and one kind grows, flowers and dies within a single year.

clue.text: The right sign, might you say?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether this is the correct symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might you say' means 'mite, as you would say it': a tick is a tiny blood-sucking mite.
explanation.definitionFit: A checkmark shows a correct answer, and the parasite that clings to dogs and sheep belongs to the mites.

clue.text: Turning up in translation

parts.note: a version is a rendering of a text in another language

explanation.surface: Something appears within a translated text.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning something upside down is turning it over, overturning.

clue.text: Give up — put editor in to change the layout

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for editor goes inside the word for give up

parts.note: to resign is to give up a post

explanation.surface: A publisher quits after an editor is brought in to rework the page design.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something anew is to rework its appearance or arrangement.

clue.text: Frightening-looking figure going round county out of control

indicators.note: the county's turned letters are placed out of, that is outside, the word for control
going round means turned about, so the county abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Worcs is the abbreviation for Worcestershire, an English county
care is charge or control, as in 'in someone's care'

explanation.surface: A scary figure is careering round the shire, out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' reverses the county abbreviation for Worcestershire to give SCROW, and 'out of' wraps it around the word for control. 'out of control' looks like an anagram signal but is not one.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw dummy dressed in old clothes is set in fields to frighten birds.

clue.text: Revered stately home — outstanding

parts.note: a country mansion is often called a Hall
an outstanding debt is one still owed

explanation.surface: A grand country house is admired as exceptional.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held sacred and greatly honoured is consecrated or venerated.

clue.text: Surplus players are gloomy

parts.note: a surplus is an amount over, left over
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: Excess actors are downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky covered with cloud is dull and dark.

clue.text: It's always hard on a servant in India

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the letter for hard comes after a

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always, as in 'for ay'
h is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Life is always tough for a domestic servant in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid or maidservant in India was called by this Anglo-Indian word.

clue.text: Generous drink goes to one's head

definitions.text: Generous drink goes to one's head

parts.words: Generous drink goes to one's head
parts.note: seemingly about strong liquor making one tipsy, but describes a brimming glass raised to the lips, filled to the top

explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a glass filled to the brim, usually for a toast, gave the adjective meaning unusually large.

clue.text: Maybe drive constituent, as important poll's closing

parts.note: grave means weighty or serious

indicators.note: closing means the final letter of poll's is taken

explanation.surface: A voter's choice matters as polling stations close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' is a driveway, which may be surfaced with small stones, not a voting drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose chips of stone are what a driveway may be made of.

clue.text: Judges' sentence, perhaps

parts.note: looks like a court's punishment, but Judges is a book of the Bible, and a sentence in it is one of its numbered units

explanation.definitionFit: Books of the Bible are divided into chapters and short numbered passages.

clue.text: Money given to gold medal winner

definitions.text: Money given to gold medal winner

parts.words: Money given to gold medal winner
parts.note: sounds like an Olympic champion's sponsorship, but describes a Nobel prizewinner, who receives a sum of money with a gold medal

explanation.definitionFit: Nobel prizewinners receive a cash award alongside their gold medal and diploma.

clue.text: He gets the pitch ready for play

definitions.text: He gets the pitch ready for play

parts.words: He gets the pitch ready for play
parts.note: suggests a groundsman preparing a sports field, but describes someone who adjusts a piano so its notes sound true

explanation.definitionFit: A piano technician adjusts strings until each note is at the correct frequency.

clue.text: Support here sounds equal

indicators.note: sounds says the word for equal is heard, not written

parts.note: a peer is an equal

explanation.surface: Someone says the backing here seems fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar holding up a bridge or arch bears its weight.

clue.text: Soft words, when grip is relaxed

indicators.note: a relaxed grip loosens its hold, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Gentle words are spoken as a hand loosens its hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxed' signals the anagram of WHEN GRIP IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech in a low hushed voice is soft talk.

clue.text: Unconscious boxer expected to lose

parts.note: someone under anaesthetic is unconscious
a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A knocked-out fighter was always tipped for defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' is the breed of dog, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitor not favoured to win is the outsider in a contest.

clue.text: Encourage artist's comeback

indicators.note: comeback means the word for artist comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a drawer is one who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone urges a painter to return to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a prize or recompense for something is to motivate more of it.
